subject: Runtime image deposit & territory addendum — questions on audit window and license activation
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@transmedhealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Rao <procurement@transmedhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy addendum — runtime image deposit, audit window, and territory scope

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security and procurement teams reviewed the MSA/Order Form and TransMed has two cross-cutting asks for private (on-prem/VPC) deployments before we can engage legal formally:

1) Runtime image deposit: We need a mechanism to obtain a "forensic runtime image" that a neutral custodian holds. The custodian would only release to TransMed upon the narrow triggers in the addendum (e.g., termination for cause, on-site forensic review). We considered traditional escrow but are open to a certified third-party custodian model.

2) Audit window & activation: Can Redwood confirm a maximum audit lookback window (ideally <= 30 days) and clarify whether audit tooling will require active agent access or if a sealed image can be used for off-line inspection? Also need clarity on whether granting temporary operator credentials is a mandatory route.

3) Territory / license activation: TransMed operates across US regions with some EU-affiliated partners. We need to ensure the Private Deploy addendum does not inadvertently broadside our localization/territory commitments in partner contracts. Any suggested language to limit license activation to the named geographies?

Attached is a short doc with our proposed triggers and a sample custodian clause. Can you share Redwood's preferred approach or redlines by COB Monday?

Best,
Alex Gomez
Head of IT Security, TransMed Health
Attachments: TransMed-PrivDeploy-Request-20260821.pdf

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@transmedhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy addendum — runtime image deposit, audit window, and territory scope

Alex — thanks for the clear note and the doc. High-level answers below; attaching a first-pass redline of the addendum for your counsel to review.

- Runtime image deposit: Redwood is open to a neutral-custodian model. We typically propose a sealed immutable snapshot (AMI/container tar + signed metadata) deposited with a mutually agreed custodian under a limited-purpose custody agreement. Release conditions in our redline are narrow (termination for cause, lawful subpoena, or mutually agreed forensic necessity). Please see section 4 of the attached redline.

- Audit window: Redwood prefers an audit lookback of 45 days by default because certain operational artifacts (logs, KV-cache fragments) may be required to reproduce issues. That said, we can offer a configuration: standard customers get 45 days; for sensitive healthcare clients we can negotiate 30 days with an agreed list of preserved artifacts. The sealed image route is compatible: we can provide a sealed snapshot plus a short-lived evidence export for on-prem forensic runs.

- Operator credentials: We consider temporary operator credentials a last resort. Our preference is: sealed snapshot + controlled witness-run process. If TransMed requires live access, we can scope a narrowly-scoped, time-limited operator role with audit trail and MFA.

- Territory: Propose explicit language tying license activation to named legal entities and cloud regions. Our draft includes a clause limiting activation to the "Named Deployment Territory" and requiring written consent for expansion.

Next steps: please have your counsel review the redline and call out any must-haves. If you prefer, I can loop our legal and product folks live to resolve the custodian language.

Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood-PrivDeploy-Addendum-draft-20260821.docx

From: Priya Rao <procurement@transmedhealth.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy addendum — runtime image deposit, audit window, and territory scope

Sean / Marissa,

Thanks — appreciate the thoughtful redline. A couple items from procurement/legal:

- Custodian model: our preference is a third-party trustee (neutral custodian) who can attest to chain-of-custody. We will share a list of approved trustees. Can Redwood accept a trustee that TransMed proposes (subject to Redwood's reasonable objection)?

- Audit window: 30 days is our target. If Redwood needs 45 days for technical reasons, can we agree to 30 days for production workloads and 45 days for historic test environments? Also request explicit limits on the scope of the forensic data that may be pulled during an audit.

- Territory: We will need a short exhibit listing the Named Deployment Territory to attach to the order form — that will avoid ambiguity.

We need legal to weigh in on the redline, but procurement will approve the custodian approach if we can: (1) confirm trustee selection process, (2) limit release triggers verbatim to the redline language, and (3) ensure Redwood keeps the snapshot and does not retain extraneous customer data beyond the ordered retention.

Will get back with counsel notes by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Priya Rao
Sr. Procurement Manager, TransMed Health

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@transmedhealth.com>, Priya Rao <procurement@transmedhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: TransMed redline coordination + proposed compromise for trustee and audit window

Team — looping legal and product on TransMed's asks. Quick summary and recommended approach so we can respond with a single, negotiated position:

Summary of asks:
- Neutral custodian / third-party trustee for a sealed runtime image deposit
- Audit lookback window target 30 days (TransMed), Redwood prefers default 45 days
- Limit license activation to Named Deployment Territory exhibit

Recommended compromise (for legal review):
1) Trustee selection: accept TransMed-proposed trustee subject to Redwood's reasonable objection within 10 business days. Add explicit acceptance criteria (security certifications, proof of chain-of-custody processes).
2) Audit window: offer tiered language — 30 days for production workloads (healthcare production), 45 days for non-production/test environments. Include explicit artifact scoping and encryption key handling to avoid over-sharing PII.
3) Sealed image custody: accept sealed runtime image deposit to trustee with signed metadata. Add strict release triggers: (a) termination for uncured breach, (b) court order/subpoena, (c) joint forensic engagement request. Any release requires written notice and a 7-business-day dispute window.
4) Territory: include a one-page Named Deployment Territory exhibit appended to the order form; require written amendment to expand.

Ask legal (Karthik/David): can you confirm whether the release triggers and dispute window wording is sufficient to protect Redwood IP and operational secrets, and whether the trustee acceptance clause needs additional guardrails? Also confirm if we can include a clause limiting Redwood's retention of the sealed image metadata to the minimum needed for verification.

I plan to send a consolidated redline to TransMed on Monday morning with the above compromise and the attached redline doc. Any material objections, escalate now.

Thanks — Sean
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
